scenes.heading: Working through content mills and marketplaces vs. direct clients

sents.d: Working through content mills and marketplaces vs. direct clients
Marketplaces are a fine place to start, a risky place to stay long-term.

Content mills and broad freelance marketplaces can be a reasonable way to get initial reps and small portfolio pieces when you have zero track record, since the barrier to entry is low and work is often available immediately.

Rates on these platforms are typically far below what direct clients pay for comparable work, since you're competing globally on price rather than on relationship or specialization — treating this as a stepping stone, not a destination, matters.

Transitioning toward direct client outreach and niche specialization as soon as you have a few portfolio pieces and testimonials usually increases both your rate and the quality of the working relationship significantly.

take: Use marketplaces briefly, then move to direct, specialized clients.
